answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits verify fraud or duplicate identities coordinating to claim rewards. Sybils are no longer free: an attacker must buy and immobilize capital for every account, and risk losing it, while honest agents can recover their bond after a clean challenge period. A bridge may relay audit proofs, but cedar and zenith should name ordinary services, not pretend to make identities unique.
